points.description: States that the table maps destination stations (MAC addresses) to outgoing LAN interfaces/links (i.e. which port a station can be reached through).

Describes backward learning: table starts empty; on receiving a frame with source address Q on LAN L, the bridge adds/updates an entry 'Q reachable via L' (optionally timestamped, old entries purged). Equivalent wording accepted.
States that in forwarding the table is looked up by destination address so frames are sent only on the matching link (selective forwarding), with flooding only when the destination is unknown.
Gives one valid benefit, e.g. less unnecessary flooding/duplication, less congestion, or better bandwidth usage.
